handled_verified.description: Node types the analyzer reads and emits from, each pinned by a fixture in validation/m14/fixtures/perl/ or by the M12 ground truth. The declaration types are the whole surface: package/class/role/sub/method declaration, variable_declaration (our/my/state/field), use_statement, use_version_statement, require_expression, require_version_expression, and assignment_expression for @ISA and the Exporter arrays; the call types are the three user-call shapes; the rest are the name-, word- and argument-bearing payload nodes reached through grammar FIELDS (name, body, signature, attributes, variable/variables, left, right, arguments, invocant, method, function, content, version, module) or through NODE TYPES. M14.6 perl wave: no node type is matched by a source-text prefix and no field is read that the pinned grammar does not declare. The pre-review counts were 6 dead node-type literals in the complexity counter (so cyclomaticComplexity was 1 for almost every real file) and 1 dead field, childForFieldName("parameters"), which shipped 0 parameters across 29,640 symbols on 5,866 files. Every one of the 52 is pinned by a fixture under validation/m14/fixtures/perl/ or by the M12 ground truth; the two decisions PERLD7/PERLD10 that also discuss container_variable and interpolated_string_literal deliberately carry no node_type claim, because both types are handled. PERL-MR4 added the last group: the node types the import-item rules read while walking a `use` argument list. `fat_comma`/`subroutine`/`anon_sub` are the shapes a `=>` or code payload takes when the grammar WRAPS it; `conditional_expression`/`logical_expression`/`match_expression`/`function_call_list_expression`/`list_call_expression`/`list_operator_expression` are the shapes a computed value takes, and the rule refuses all of them because CODE IS NOT NAMES -- a `?:` branch or a call argument is computed at runtime, so it cannot be an imported name. `parenthesized_expression` does not exist in the wired 1.2.1 grammar at all; it is registered for the same reason `noninterpolated_string_content` is -- the lane reads BOTH generations, and a grammar bump must not silently introduce a type that the audit would then call unknown. Every one of these 10 was caught by the F1 grammar cell the moment it was referenced without registration, which is the cell doing its job.

internal_silent.description: Operators, literals, expression payload and containers — each either walked for the calls nested inside it or correctly emitting nothing. The statement wrappers (expression_statement, 320,936 corpus sites) and block_statement are pure containers; comment, escape_sequence and interpolated_string_literal are payload. Variable READS are container_variable (28,140 sites) plus the element/deref/slice forms: this lane's compared relationship set has no `uses` label, so a read is not an edge — a declared ontology decision, recorded as PERLD7, not an oversight. Counts are from the 7-corpus census (5,866 files: mojo, plack, perl5 core, Moose, Moo, Catalyst-Runtime, DBI). ERROR and MISSING are included deliberately: tree-sitter's error-recovery nodes are not declared by this grammar and never appear in `nodeTypeForId`, but every parser emits them on a malformed file, and the analyzer DOES consult them — 55 corpus files carry 619 of them and a lane that called them unclassified would be claiming it never sees one. Ten other lanes classify the same pair (bash, css, fsharp, hcl, html, java, javascript, kotlin, make, markdown) and script/m14/completeness-inventory.ts appends the pair to every lane's type list on purpose, because a spec that classifies ERROR correctly was once told its own row was grammar drift. Silent here means: walked, produces no symbol and no relationship, and its children are still descended so a declaration inside a damaged file is not lost.

gap.description: All confirmed gaps closed as of 2026-09-27 (M14.6 perl wave).

design_decision.description: Owner rulings — never silent absence. A decision's `node_type` claims the grammar types it rules; types with no claim here are classified in handled_verified or internal_silent instead, and a type appears in EXACTLY ONE bucket across all four.

decisions.question: Is a named list operator (`print`, `fork`, `time`) a call edge?
decisions.resolution: No, and the suppression is DERIVED rather than hand-listed: PERL_BUILTINS is the union of the grammar's own fixed op-token sets — the words it will parse as func0op/func1op rather than as an arbitrary bareword call — and the named-op entries of perl 5.38's opcode.h, minus the words that can never be a call target. 2,895 corpus sites, 0 edges. The pre-review list was 10 words short, and `say` and `system` alone produced phantom call edges on mojo.

decisions.question: Is a named unary operator (`length`, `chr`, `say`) a call edge?
decisions.resolution: No — same derivation as PERLD1, which is why the two are one rule and not two hand-lists. 42,998 corpus sites, 0 edges. A word in that set is a call the LANGUAGE owns, so naming it would invent an edge to a symbol that does not exist.

decisions.question: Do BEGIN / END / INIT / CHECK declare a symbol?
decisions.resolution: No. A phaser is a compile-time hook with no name a user can navigate to, and nothing can call it. 3,143 corpus sites. The same ruling covers class_phaser_statement (ADJUST / STRINGIFY in a 5.38 class body), which has 0 sites in 5,866 files — recorded so the ruling is not mistaken for an untested assumption.

decisions.question: Should the `:prototype(@)` value of an attribute be published?
decisions.resolution: No. The attribute NAME is emitted as `decorators` on the sub — the AST contract's carrier, which the production pool worker forwards to brain_symbol. The value is the prototype's payload and names no symbol. 1,072 corpus sites.

decisions.question: Does `LABEL: sub f {}` need a symbol for the label?
decisions.resolution: No. The sub is emitted through its own `name` field — verified on a fixture — and the label would be a second symbol for one declaration. 1,210 corpus sites of each of statement_label and identifier; a label names a goto target, not a declaration.

decisions.question: Should `sub f(ident $x)` publish a parameter symbol?
decisions.resolution: No. 4 corpus sites in 5,866 files, and this is an INVOCATION form rather than a declaration; a symbol per named parameter would invent API surface. The signature's mandatory / optional / slurpy parameters ARE published on the sub — 40 subs with a real signature across the census, against 0 before this wave.

decisions.question: Should a variable read be a `uses` edge?
decisions.resolution: No. This lane's compared relationship set is extends / implements / instantiates / overrides / calls / contains; there is no `uses` label for perl, so a read is not an edge. 28,140 corpus sites of container_variable alone. This is an ONTOLOGY ruling, and it is the same fact that made `contains` have to JOIN the compared set for this lane: the harness filters the truth side only, so a truth label outside the set can never be covered and would read as a permanent false MISSING.
decisions.classification_note: container_variable is classified in handled_verified, not here: the analyzer DOES read it (it declares `my @rest` / `%seen` variables and their ranges). The ruling is about the EDGE, not the node — a bare container read emits no `uses`, because a perl variable's storage is not resolvable across files without a dataflow pass this lane does not have.

decisions.question: Do the 5.32-5.36 control constructs declare symbols?
decisions.resolution: No. `defer {}`, `async {}` and `await` execute a block or are an operator; none has an invocable name. Measured 0, 8 and 17 corpus sites respectively — recorded so the ruling is not mistaken for an untested assumption.

decisions.question: Is the group node of `our ($a, $b) = ...` a declaration?
decisions.resolution: No. It is transparent: its members are read through the `variable` / `variables` FIELDS, which is also the only correct read under this grammar — the parenthesised form spells the field `variables` and the bare form `variable`, 25,750 and 0 sites respectively. 0 corpus sites for the group node itself, classified so the type can never be silently absent.

decisions.question: How are the words of a double-quoted literal read?
decisions.resolution: Through grammar FIELDS and node types, never by pattern: the `content` field where the grammar declares one, otherwise the `string_content` children. For a double-quoted literal ONLY the string_content pieces are words, so `use lib "./t/lib"` publishes `./t/lib` and never an interpolated `$dir`. The type is handled_verified (it is read); this ruling records WHICH of its children count. Unread before this wave, so every double-quoted import argument lost its items — `use feature "class"`, `use lib "./t/lib"`, `use warnings "once"`.
decisions.classification_note: interpolated_string_literal is classified in handled_verified, not here. It was unhandled when this ruling was written and is handled now: perlWordValues reads string_content / noninterpolated_string_content, which is what recovered `use feature "class"` and `use lib "./t/lib"`. The ruling below records the contract that fix obeys.

decisions.question: Does a `format` block declare a symbol?
decisions.resolution: No. 5 corpus sites in 5,866 files; the format body is string payload and declares no name.

decisions.question: Which relationship kinds does the perl lane owe, given that it emits no `uses`, `references`, `imports` or `exports` EDGE?
decisions.resolution: DECLARED: the six the analyzer emits are calls, contains, extends, implements, instantiates and overrides. `uses`/`references` are NOT emitted: a perl call site names a bareword or a method, and neither resolves to a file-level definition without an inter-file symbol table the lane does not have — the honest edge is `calls` to the name, and the indexer resolves it later. Perl's dependency surface is the `imports` payload (ImportInfo rows the store materialises) plus the Module Includes pattern, not a relationship. Omitting these from requiredKinds is a ruling, not an oversight: they appear in LANG_CONFIGS.perl.requiredKinds only as the six that exist.

decisions.question: Is `overrides` a source-derived fact for perl?
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION: `overrides` is the lane's ONLY guessed relationship. It is inferred from a first-parent chain at confidence 0.5, so it can never clear a 0.7 structural floor, and classifyEvidenceTier therefore labels it `inferred` on its own without a special case. A perl class may inherit from several bases, and only the first is consulted — a method that overrides a method of the SECOND base is not an override edge. Fixtures pin confidence 0.5 AND line_number: null (validation/m14/fixtures/perl/inheritance.expectation.json), because a guess has no source line.

decisions.question: Is the 168-vs-140 node-type count a stale row?
decisions.resolution: NO. tree-sitter-perl.wasm 1.2.1 declares 168 NAMED NODE-TYPE IDs that resolve to 140 UNIQUE names (a supertype/hidden-alias family shares ids). The gate's message prints the ID count; the spec classifies all 140 NAMES, each exactly once. Both numbers are correct and mean different things — do not 'fix' the 140 in docs/analyzers/real-perl-analyzer.md to match the gate's 168.
